On Mon, Apr 15, 2028 at 10:30 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marissa / Jonas — looping you both in to draft the CSV mapping and runbook.

Hi all — quick answers and an initial artifact attached (residency_mapping.csv).

Scope assumption: for CloudFolio marketplace listings we typically consider the following artifact classes: 
- Customer prompts & chat state (user-submitted content)
- Generated outputs (responses)
- Model usage logs and token-level telemetry
- Embeddings and derived vectors (if customer enables vector storage)
- Backups / periodic snapshots of persistent stores

Default retention windows:
- Prompts & responses: 30 days (default), configurable down to 0/ephemeral or up to 365 days under contract
- Usage logs/telemetry: 90 days standard, archived up to 2 years for enterprise compliance on request
- Embeddings: 365 days by default unless customer elects no-storage mode
- Backups/snapshots: retained 30 days, encrypted and region-scoped

Deletion workflow (summary):
1) Request received (API or portal) -> deletion job scheduled
2) Live data removed from application stores within SLA window (24–72 hours depending on size)
3) Background compaction + key rotation to prevent access to residuals
4) Snapshot/backups expired or deleted per schedule (up to additional 7 days)
5) Audit log entry generated, runbook emits deletion certificate once job completes

We have an internal SOC2-aligned evidence package we can extract showing deletion job timestamps and audit log snapshots. I’ve attached a CSV with region -> service endpoint mapping for AWS/GCP/Azure; this maps Redwood logical regions to provider endpoints (first-pass).

Questions for CloudFolio: do you require deletion certificates to include a per-account UUID and timestamp, or is a signed runbook + audit excerpt acceptable?

Attaching: residency_mapping.csv (stub)

—
Marissa Cole
Sr. TPM, Platform Compliance

Marissa / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached are our redlines (cloudfolio_redlines.docx). A few legal asks we need addressed before we can finalize the listing agreement: 

1) Deletion attestation frequency — we need an option for a per-customer deletion certificate (UUID, deletion timestamps, hashes of deleted blobs) or a contractual statement that Redwood will provide deletion certificates upon request within 7 business days.
2) Retention exceptions — we require clarity about legal holds and whether Redwood will support a customer-specific retention override on a contract-by-contract basis.
3) Proof of in-region backups — can you confirm backups are created and stored in the selected provider region and that cross-region replicas are disabled unless explicitly elected?

Please note: we’ve flagged SOC2 artifact requests under section 4.2 of our checklist. We’d like to see a redacted example of the deletion certificate and a sample deletion audit excerpt. If possible, please attach a runbook and a short chart showing time-to-delete measurements for a typical 1TB dataset (estimate).

Regards,
Partner Legal
CloudFolio

Hi — we consolidated answers and attached a short deletion playbook (deletion_runbook_v1.pdf) and the redacted certificate template. Links below:

- Residency mapping (first-pass): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cResidencyPlaybooks
- DocuSign for Contract Addendum (if you want the per-customer certificate clause): https://na1.docusign.net/Signing/?s=abc123def
- HubSpot record: HS-76342 (notes and attachments)

Short answers to legal asks: 
1) Deletion attestation: we can provide per-customer deletion certificates (UUID + timestamps + audit excerpt). Standard turnaround: 7 business days. If CloudFolio requires a guaranteed SLA for certificate delivery, we can add a clause to the addendum and automate certificate emission for a fee.
2) Retention exceptions / legal holds: Redwood supports contract-level retention overrides. Legal holds are supported via a hold flag; deletion jobs will skip held accounts and we emit separate audit entries.
3) Backups: by default backups are created in-region and cross-region replicas are disabled unless the customer enables cross-region DR. We call this out in the attachment.

Next steps: 
- Please confirm whether you want per-customer certificates to be included in the contract (we’ll prepare a DocuSign amendment).
- Sara — once you confirm scope and whether CloudOps needs the 1TB time-to-delete benchmark, we’ll run a test and provide measurements (target by 04/26).

Forwarded attachments: deletion_runbook_v1.pdf (summary + runbook), redacted_certificate_template.pdf (stub).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
